facts.text: Benicia was founded May 19 1847 and became the third city incorporated in California in 1851.
The city was named after Francisca Benicia Carillo de Vallejo, the wife of General Mariano Vallejo, whose second given name was used when 'Francisca' was dropped.
Benicia served as California's state capital for nearly thirteen months from 1853 to 1854, and the old capitol building now sits in a state historic park.
In 1879 the Central Pacific Railroad rerouted its transcontinental line through Benicia, establishing a major ferry across the Carquinez Strait to Port Costa.
The original campus of Mills College, the first women's college west of the Rockies, opened in Benicia in 1852 as the Young Ladies Seminary.
Benicia’s historic Arsenal, reauthorized by Lincoln in 1862, became the first military ordnance depot on the West Coast, supplying conflicts through the Korean War.
